encoder: Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), working alone for Legalese; no subagents, no independent test pass
display_name: Mishnah Kinnim: the whole tractate, with 3:2's majority as Koppel and Reiss read it beside three older readings, a seat for the person who brought the birds, and solver obligations
maintainer: legalese (no named individual has taken it)
seat: the person who brought the birds (a woman after childbirth, a man or woman after a discharge, or anyone who vowed or gave a bird offering), or her heir, asking how many of her offerings were or may be validly offered and what she must bring again; the priest is an official and has no seat
generated_from: the six rule modules are generated from tools/*.l4.in by tools/render.py, which pastes each {{Q ID N M}} quotation from ../../registers/source-bundle/ with srcrefs.py quoteid; re-rendering on 2026-11-02 reproduced all six byte for byte

scope.edition: Mishnah Kinnim, the printed text (נוסח הדפוסים) as he.wikisource renders it, standard numbering (4, 5 and 6 units), page revisions 2874944, 2874946 and 2874949, read 2026-11-02; aids: Maimonides' recension (5, 6, 5), Bartenura on chapters 1-3, Tiferet Yisrael on chapter 3 (OCR), Maimonides, Pesulei ha-Mukdashin 8. Crosswalks to Maimonides' and Koppel's numbering are in NOTES.md.
scope.encoded: every unit, in the sense of the coverage table in NOTES.md: 23 rows, 22 encoded; 3:2 under four readings of 'the majority' (Koppel and Reiss, taken; Bartenura; Tiferet Yisrael; Maimonides) and a search over every apportionment that checks the formula; 2:3 under Bartenura's decree, checked against all three of the text's tables.
scope.not_encoded: inert: 3:6's closing aggadah (Rabbi Yehoshua's ram; Rabbi Shimon ben Akashya), quoted with no rule. No unit is deferred.
scope.not_answerable: a priest who put some other number above than all, none or half (NOTHING; a separate rule labelled 'beyond the text' gives the worst case); Bartenura's and Maimonides' readings of 3:2 for more than two owners (NOTHING); whether a bird of an obligation that died or was stolen must be replaced (NOTHING: the text is silent); the derivations of 3:6's last two cases (the text's numbers are encoded as given). The forks behind them are F1 to F10 in NOTES.md.

not_reviewed: No domain expert has read this encoding against the text, no independent test author has written tests for it, and Moshe Koppel's own article (Higayon 2, pp. 96-102) and book (Seder Kinnim, 1998) were not obtained: his reading is known through Reiss (Torah u-Madda Journal 9, 2000, n. 29) and Beller (Higayon 5, pp. 155-157).
